name: Belonger Status by Descent/Parentage

qualifying_event.description: A person whose parent(s) were born in Anguilla or hold Belonger status may apply to the Immigration Department for Belonger Status by descent/parentage.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Applicant's and parent(s)' birth certificates; parents' marriage certificate if applicable at time of birth; Belonger Certificate.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires parent(s) born in Anguilla or holding Belonger status, proven via the applicant's birth certificate (which must include the father's name), the parent(s)' birth certificates, a Belonger Certificate, and the parents' marriage certificate if applicable at the time of the applicant's birth.

evidence_required.document: Applicant's birth certificate (must include father's name)
Marriage certificate (if applicable at time of birth)

sources.title: Government of Anguilla -- Anguilla Status (Belonger Status): descent/parentage, marriage (5 years), and residence (15 years) grounds, documents, and fees

Government of Anguilla -- Immigration Forms: separate Belonger Status application forms for Great Grandchild-Parentage, Born in Anguilla and resident for 10 or 15 years, Children of Applicant, Marriage of 5 years, and a General Application Form

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Anguilla's initial build, and the first British Overseas Territory (BOT) built this session -- this is an architecturally different case from every prior country and required a deliberate, non-obvious modelling decision explained here once. Anguilla is not a sovereign state: it has no citizenship of its own. 'Belonger Status' is Anguilla's own local legal status (akin to a right of abode/local nationality), while formal British nationality is held separately as a British Overseas Territories Citizen (BOTC), acquired through a distinct naturalisation process (see ai_naturalisation.json) that does not require Belonger Status as a precondition -- the naturalisation-tips source requires a Permanent Resident Permit, not a Belonger Certificate. Because of this, every Belonger Status route in this dataset (this file, ai_belonger_status_marriage.json, ai_belonger_status_residence.json) models leads_to_citizenship as false, even though Belonger Status functions as the practical 'you belong here' status and would, in a sovereign-state dataset entry, likely have been modelled as leading to citizenship. This is a deliberate departure from how ancestry/family/settled routes are modelled for every other country built this session, and should be read before comparing Anguilla's data to other countries'. The immigration-forms page also lists a 'Great Grandchild-Parentage' form as a distinct variant from the general parentage form used here -- the anguilla-status page content did not separately detail different requirements for great-grandchild-degree descent, so this is modelled as a single descent route; the possible distinction is flagged, not resolved.
